result.rule: When the description says a sending step transmits several information items at once, and at least one of those items must be supplied through a separate action by a participant that is not part of the sending step itself: Model the supplying action as its own manual task, performed by the participant who supplies the item, and model each other preparatory action as its own task. Open the preparatory branches with a parallel gateway placed before the first preparatory task, and close them with a matching parallel gateway placed before the sending task, so the send can only proceed once every supply is done. Do not merge the supply into the describing task or the sending task, and do not join these branches with an exclusive gateway.

When the description states that one or more items are passed from one set of participants to another set of participants, who then perform a stated activity on those items, so the passing-on occurs as a step before that activity: Model the passing-on as its own manual task, performed by a human participant and not by a system, placed after the step that prepares the items and before the receiving participants' activity. Model the receiving participants' activity as a separate following task. Do not omit the passing-on step, and do not merge it into the label of the activity task.

When the description states that a set of selected items each receive a notification or request to take part, and that each item's own choice then determines which of several follow-up paths is taken: Model the notification or request sent to the selected items as its own task, placed on the sequence flow after the preceding step and before the gateway that splits on each item's choice. Do not drop this action, and do not connect the preceding task directly to the choice gateway.

When the description has a step of one role whose result is passed to a different role, and the receiving role then performs its own described step as a task in its own pool (for example, a role that is asked to act on information or an item another role has sent): Model the receiving step as a task in the receiving role's pool and draw a message flow from the sending step in the sender's pool to that receiving task, with the arrow pointing from sender to receiver. Do not replace this flow with one that ends at a catch event when the receiver's described step is a performed task, and do not reverse the arrow direction.

args.text: the description says a single later sending step transmits several information items together, and at least one of those items must first be supplied by a separate action performed by a participant who is not part of the sending step

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already covers the multi-item send with a preparatory supply action before deciding the relation to the learned rule.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
